title: "Tracing Concepts"
description: "A worked microservices lesson using one small shop example."

**Course source:** Day 3 §4.1–§4.2. The running application contains Product, Order and User services.

## Logs from one service are not enough

A request enters Gateway, reaches Order and fans out to Product and User. Each service may log a successful request, yet the overall checkout can still be slow. The course introduces distributed tracing to reconstruct this **cross-service causal path**.

~~~text
Trace 8af...
  Gateway span          0–120 ms
    Order span          10–115 ms
      Product HTTP      20–105 ms
      User HTTP         22–35 ms
~~~

A **trace** represents one logical operation; a **span** represents one timed operation within it, usually with a parent-child relationship. A trace ID connects operations; a span ID identifies a particular operation.

## Propagating context

Gateway must pass trace context to Order, and Order must pass it into outgoing Product/User requests. Without propagation, every service may create a separate trace and the viewer cannot reconstruct the path.

The lab propagates a simplified `x-trace-id` header for teaching. A real tracing implementation should use interoperable trace-context standards and library instrumentation rather than inventing its own header protocol.

## Instrument key boundaries

Create server spans for inbound HTTP and client spans for outgoing HTTP. Add safe attributes such as route, service, HTTP status and error category. Avoid collecting credentials, secret values or customer data in span attributes.

## Trace and logs complement each other

Traces show the **shape and timing** of one request. Metrics aggregate behaviour across all requests. Logs provide detailed local events. Consistent context IDs let an operator move between these views.

## Legacy naming

The course introduces Spring Cloud Sleuth. Modern Spring observability commonly uses **Micrometer Tracing**, which succeeded Sleuth; the tracing concepts themselves remain stable.

[Micrometer Tracing](https://docs.micrometer.io/tracing/reference/) · [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/signals/traces/).

## Check your understanding

Explain the request or event path end to end. Which component can fail, and which information would you collect to diagnose that failure?
